run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T08:49:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert is firing because frontend-proxy's ingress listener really does return errors: in the hour ending 2026-11-17T08:56:41Z its `ingress` spans carried STATUS_CODE_ERROR 31.48 times against 22,490 UNSET spans, and every one of the 31 failing request lines I read from the frontend-proxy access log (08:22:33Z–08:53:01Z) is an HTTP 503 with response flag `UC` and response-code details `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` toward the `frontend` upstream (100.70.94.93:8080), with 0 bytes received from upstream and no upstream service time — i.e. the connection died before the frontend answered. Errors are sporadic (~1 per 40–90 s, at most ~6.7 per 2-minute bucket) and hit every route (GET /, /api/cart, /api/products/*, /api/recommendations, /api/data), which points at a connection-level fault on the frontend side rather than a route bug. The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, no last termination, no OOMKill, and its own spans record zero ERROR status for the whole window, so the resets are not visible in the frontend's own telemetry. I could not establish a baseline: the traces metric has no samples at all before ~08:22:00Z, and the alert's own rule is not loaded in this Prometheus, so whether the error rate rose before 08:49:19Z is unknown. The leading hypothesis for why the frontend connection is terminated is a keep-alive race between Envoy's reused upstream connection and the frontend HTTP server closing it; CPU/memory starvation of the frontend (limit 100m CPU / 200Mi) remains an untested alternative because no container CPU or throttling metrics exist here. Checked and not implicated: flagd fault flags (all defaultVariant "off"), node i-030aedeb6471c8a81 (Ready, no pressure conditions), and the fraud-detection OOMKill at 08:14:48Z (different call path, no frontend/checkout error spans).

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error signal is nonzero during the window: increase of traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=frontend-proxy, span_name=ingress, status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR was 31.484 in the hour ending 2026-11-17T08:56:41Z versus 22,490 for STATUS_CODE_UNSET (about 0.14% of ingress spans), which matches the alert annotation's condition of an error rate above 0.

All 31 error lines I read from the frontend-proxy access log (between 2026-11-17T08:22:33Z and 08:53:01Z) are HTTP 503 with response flag `UC` and response-code details `upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}`, upstream cluster `frontend`, 0 bytes received, 95 bytes sent and no upstream service time; they cover many different routes (GET /, GET /api/cart, GET /api/products/*, GET /api/recommendations?..., GET /api/data/?...).

In the same access log the successful frontend-proxy requests show the `frontend` upstream host as 100.70.94.93:8080 (the frontend Service address) and the downstream peer as 100.96.2.17, which is the load-generator pod; the failing 503 lines name the same upstream cluster and host, so the failed connections were to the frontend Service, not to another dependency.

The frontend Service has exactly one ready endpoint: Deployment frontend is 1/1 ready with a single ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 and a single pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (pod IP 100.96.2.139, all conditions True including Ready), and frontend-proxy likewise runs as one pod.

The frontend-proxy errors are continuous but sporadic across the window, not a single spike at the alert time: 120s buckets show nonzero error increase in every bucket from 08:23:19Z to 08:55:19Z with a maximum of about 6.7 errors per bucket, and 2-minute rate points from 08:37:19Z to 08:55:19Z range from 0 to about 6.7.

The frontend pod is healthy on Kubernetes terms and shows no crash: frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh (created 2026-11-17T08:09:24Z, node i-030aedeb6471c8a81, limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi) has restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt (created 08:09:23Z, limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi) also has restartCount 0 with no previous container instance.

The frontend service's own spans record no errors during the window: every frontend operation shown for service_name=frontend (GET, POST, GET /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/*, grpc.oteldemo.*, tcp.connect) has STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0, while the corresponding frontend-proxy ingress series is nonzero.

No pre-alert baseline exists for the frontend-proxy traces metric: a query over 08:09:00Z–08:24:00Z returned source_start_at 08:22:00Z, i.e. no samples before about 08:22Z, and an instant query of the error increase at 07:50:00Z returned no data at all.

At the alert anchor instant 08:49:19Z the summed 5-minute error-span rate for frontend-proxy was 0.0111 per second, while the 1-minute rate evaluated at the same instant was 0; the annotation's value 0.0333 could not be reproduced from these two windows.

No injected fault is declared as active: every flag in the flagd-config ConfigMap (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

The node hosting both frontend and frontend-proxy, i-030aedeb6471c8a81, reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False, so node-level pressure is not present at query time.

The events returned for the window contain only data-recorders objects (pods/jobs/PVCs/statefulsets/deployment there, e.g. SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Started, ProvisioningSucceeded); no event involving an otel-demo object was returned, so there is no kubelet event documenting an otel-demo failure in this window.

A change did occur during the window on a different component: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wvrwx has restartCount 1 and its previous container terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-17T08:14:48Z; it is currently Running and Ready.

All 21 otel-demo pods, including frontend and frontend-proxy, carry creationTimestamps between 2026-11-17T08:09:22Z and 08:11:16Z, i.e. they predate the alert (08:49:19Z) but were created inside the authorized window.

Leading explanation for the 503s: the frontend HTTP server in pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh closes idle keep-alive connections while Envoy reuses one of them, so Envoy reports upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} with zero upstream response bytes on an otherwise healthy, never-restarted frontend. It fits the sporadic ~1-per-40-90s pattern, the sub-millisecond-to-sub-second failures, the fact that all routes are affected equally, and the absence of any error span in the frontend service itself; it is not confirmed because neither the Envoy upstream idle-timeout configuration nor the frontend keep-alive settings are readable (Envoy config is image-baked, no ConfigMap for it, and the frontend container writes no log lines).

Alternative cause not testable here: the frontend container's tight limits (cpu 100m, memory 200Mi) could make the Next.js process drop or fail connections under the ~15 requests/second load; no container CPU, throttling or memory-working-set series exist in this Prometheus (kube_pod_container_status*/kube_pod_status* returned nothing), so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Secondary alternative: frontend-proxy's own very small limits (cpu 30m, memory 50Mi) could contribute to failures in the proxy, but every failing request I read carries an upstream-originated reset detail rather than a listener or connection-pool error, so the fault is attributed to the upstream side rather than to Envoy itself.

Fault injection via flagd is not the cause: every flag in flagd-config has defaultVariant "off", and none of the declared faults (adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, productCatalogFailure, etc.) would produce connection_termination resets at the Envoy-to-frontend hop.

The fraud-detection OOMKill at 08:14:48Z is not the cause of this alert: the failing requests are on the frontend hop for all routes (including GET / and /api/products/*), which does not traverse fraud-detection, and the checkout, payment and frontend series in this window show zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase, so no observed failure path links that restart to the frontend-proxy 503s.

Node-level resource pressure as the origin is contradicted: node i-030aedeb6471c8a81 (host of frontend and frontend-proxy) is Ready with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False.

Frontend pod instability as such is contradicted for the visible window: frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, an empty lastState (no OOMKilled, no terminated reason), a single ReplicaSet with no second generation, and its own spans never carry an error status.

Advisory: compare the Envoy upstream idle timeout / connection pool settings in the frontend-proxy bootstrap config with the frontend HTTP server keep-alive settings (and consider enabling frontend container stdout logging), because the evidence pattern is a reused-connection race that neither side's configuration could be read in this run.

Advisory: add container CPU-throttling / memory-working-set series (cAdvisor or kube-state-metrics equivalents) so the frontend (100m CPU / 200Mi) and frontend-proxy (30m CPU / 50Mi) resource hypotheses can be tested, and review the alert rule that produced value 0.0333, since no RequestErrorRate rule is loaded in this Prometheus and the value could not be reproduced.

gaps: The alerting rule behind RequestErrorRate is not present in this Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate and with type=alert both returned no data, so the rule expression, its threshold and its evaluation window are unknown and the reported value 0.0333 could not be reproduced (measured 5m rate 0.0111/s and 1m rate 0 at 2026-11-17T08:49:19Z).

No baseline before the alert deviation: traces_span_metrics_calls_total for frontend-proxy has no samples before about 2026-11-17T08:22:00Z (a query over 08:09–08:24 returned source_start_at 08:22:00Z, and instant queries at 07:50:00Z and earlier returned no data), so it is unknown whether the error rate was zero before 08:49:19Z or had been nonzero since the pods started at 08:09Z; no latency trend is claimed for the same reason.

The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr lines at all (0 lines read for pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh, both current and previous instances), so the application-side reason for closing the connections could not be read.

The frontend-proxy (Envoy) bootstrap configuration is not stored in any readable ConfigMap (only flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector, product-catalog-products exist in otel-demo), so upstream idle timeouts, keep-alive settings and connection pool limits could not be verified.

frontend-proxy access-log history before 2026-11-17T08:22:33Z could not be read (the 4 MiB per-read limit was reached and older lines were dropped), so whether 503 `UC` responses existed earlier in the window is unknown.

Container CPU usage, CPU throttling and memory working-set metrics are unavailable in this Prometheus (no kube_pod_status_* or kube_pod_container_status_* series returned), so resource-starvation hypotheses for the frontend (100m CPU / 200Mi) and frontend-proxy (30m CPU / 50Mi) remain untested.

Caller-side impact is unverified: the proxy access log shows the load-generator pod (100.96.2.17) as the downstream peer of the failing requests, but load-generator logs and client-side error counts were not checked, so customer-visible impact is not established.

No events involving otel-demo objects were returned (the event grouping contained only data-recorders objects), so the fraud-detection OOMKill at 08:14:48Z has no accompanying event in the returned set; events may have expired and their absence is not proof nothing happened.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so nothing can be said about configuration or deployment changes preceding the alert.
next_steps: Inspect the frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap configuration for upstream idle_timeout, per-connection buffer limits and HTTP/1.1 keep-alive settings, and compare them with the frontend server's keep-alive/headers timeouts.
Enable or capture frontend container logs (and, if possible, a packet/connection-level trace) to confirm whether the resets originate from the frontend HTTP server closing idle connections.

Correlate the failing request IDs from the frontend-proxy access log (e.g. 5032fb49-081b-9ab0-b74e-6afae142391e, b4c542c8-529c-9c0f-bb48-c1a2569c7505) against frontend-side request handling to see whether the frontend ever received them.
Review the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the alerting system that produced this alert, and consider whether an alert threshold of above 0 on sporadic connection resets is intentional.
Collect cAdvisor CPU throttling and memory working-set series for frontend and frontend-proxy to test the resource-limit hypotheses.
